answer:
Yes. NovaLearn should keep the Advanced OCR Pipeline ahead of the Microsoft Teams integration, based on the corpus.

- The Advanced OCR Pipeline is already designated as NovaLearn’s highest technical priority because scanned policy documents are the primary driver of citation errors and customer onboarding delays [NL-001#NL-001-S08].
- The CTO argues that engineering is fully committed to the OCR pipeline and that it is a critical system stability requirement, noting that 27% of May support tickets related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- The Product lead agrees that delivering a Teams integration before fixing ingestion and citation problems would just deliver inaccurate, un-cited answers to a larger audience inside the chat app, so the OCR pipeline must remain the top priority for August [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- Rushing Teams also creates security risk: a Teams bot supporting logical workspace isolation and RBAC requires a complete redesign of the auth layer, and a premature launch could risk tenant-isolation breach and security certification [NL-015#NL-015-S06].
- The approved talk track positions NovaLearn’s Teams integration for Q4 2026 and emphasizes that secure retrieval is the only way to deploy AI in the enterprise [NL-032#NL-032-S05].
- Teams is the most common feature request and is in high demand [NL-011#NL-011-S07], but the roadmap targets design in Q4 2026, with the OCR pipeline scheduled for August 2026 [NL-001#NL-001-S08] [NL-015#NL-015-S06].

Business recommendation: fix OCR and citation accuracy first, then deliver Teams as a secure, permission-enforcing integration. This protects the enterprise trust position and avoids scaling broken answers across a broader channel.
